newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge up 0.31 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge up 0.31 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended slightly firmer on Friday amid selective and narrow trade, despite earlier profit-taking, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at this week's fourth all-time high of 1,918, up six points, or 0.31 percent from Thursday's previous record of 1,912.
Today's was the sixth record since late June when hopes of a secularist coalition boosted the market.
Over the week, it gained 5.67 percent on top of last week's 10.5 percent surge prompted by political optimism.
A right-left coalition headed by conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz was formed on Monday, to replace the former Islamist-led coalition.
Expectations that the new government will win a confidence vote in parliament on July 12 are widespread.
Trade volume firmed to 29.69 trillion lira ($197.6 million) from Thursday's 27.48 trillion ($183.9 million).
